title: A little time outside
body: If it feels manageable, try a short walk on a familiar route. Ten minutes is an option, not a target. You can turn back whenever you like.

title: A gentler end to the day
body: You could choose one quiet activity before bed, such as putting your phone aside or dimming a light. Keep it simple and familiar. Notice what feels helpful for you.

title: One small task
body: Pick one manageable piece of something on your list. You can stop after that piece. Finishing everything today is not the goal.

title: Notice what is around you
body: If you would like, name five things you can see, four you can feel, three you can hear, two you can smell and one you can taste. Skip any sense that is uncomfortable or inaccessible. Stop whenever you want.

title: A small hello
body: You could send a person you trust a short hello or ask if they have time to talk. You can share as much or as little as feels comfortable. A message can be a first step.

title: Something simple to eat
body: An easy, familiar meal may be a manageable next step. It does not have to be elaborate. You could ask someone you trust to share a meal with you.

title: Three lines are enough
body: Try a line about what happened, one about how today felt, and one about what would help next. Short notes count. You can leave a line blank.

title: A free place to talk
body: Tele-MANAS is a free government helpline available around the clock at 14416. Support is available in English and 20 regional languages. You can ask about support options near you.

title: Your first appointment
body: You can ask how sessions work, what they cost, and how your information is kept private. You decide what you want to share. If the fit does not feel right, you can explore another provider.

title: Ask about costs first
body: Fees vary by city and provider; ask about a sliding scale and public options. Tele-MANAS is free, and government hospital OPD fees can be free or low. The Mental Healthcare Act 2017 section 21(4) sets insurance parity, but outpatient visits may not be covered, so check your own policy before booking.
